How an Iowa property tax bill is worked out

The county assessor sets an assessed value, a state percentage called the rollback turns that into taxable value, and local levy rates are applied to the taxable value. The result is the tax bill for the parcel.

Iowa Code 441.21 values property at actual value, meaning fair and reasonable market value between a willing buyer and a willing seller, and generally assesses it at 100 percent of that figure. Sales of the property or comparable property in normal transactions must be taken into account. Abnormal sales are excluded or adjusted, and the statute names sales to immediate family, foreclosures and other forced sales, contract sales and discounted purchases as examples.

For homes, "residential" means property used mainly for habitation with two or fewer dwelling units, plus a few other housing types. A duplex and a single-family house therefore fall in the same class.

The rollback and taxable value

The rollback is a percentage the Iowa Department of Revenue certifies each year to limit growth in assessments. Taxable value is the assessed value multiplied by that percentage.

The idea sits in 441.21 even though the word does not appear: residential and agricultural growth is tied together, so one class can rise only as fast as the other if the other grows more slowly. Iowa first enacted a rollback in 1977, and the department certifies the limitation percentages to county auditors each November.

When you compare two Iowa tax statements, read both the assessed value line and the taxable value line. A seller who sees assessed value rise can still see a smaller change in taxable value.

Due dates and penalties

Iowa property taxes are paid in two halves, and each half becomes delinquent on a set date. The first half is due before September 1 and becomes delinquent October 1. The second half is due before March 1 and becomes delinquent April 1 (445.36 and 445.37).

Tax eventRule
First installmentDelinquent October 1, or the second business day of October if September 30 falls on a weekend
Second installmentDelinquent April 1, or the second business day of April if March 31 falls on a weekend
Delinquent interest1.5% per month, any part of a month counts as a full month
Delinquent noticeTreasurer notifies taxpayers if an installment is unpaid on November 1
Refund claim for erroneous paymentWithin two years of the due date or a final appeal decision
Annual tax saleThird Monday in June

A payment must reach the treasurer by the last business day of the month before the delinquency date, or be postmarked before it. A missing statement does not excuse nonpayment. Interest is in 445.39, the notice in 445.36, the refund claim in 445.60 and the sale date in 446.7.

What changed for homeowners under the 2026 tax law?

Senate File 2472 replaces the homestead tax credit with an exemption equal to 10% of the homestead's taxable value. Division 20 of the 2026 Iowa Acts was signed on May 18, 2026.

  • The old credit equaled the tax on $4,850 of value. The new exemption has a $5,500 minimum and a $20,000 maximum in taxable value.
  • The maximum will be adjusted for inflation starting with assessment years on or after January 1, 2027.
  • The change applies to assessment year 2026, so the benefit shows up in taxes paid in September 2027 and March 2028.
  • The disabled veteran homestead credit remains in place for eligible owners.

The bill also sets a roughly 2% annual growth limit on most general levies for budgets beginning July 1, 2027, a lower school foundation levy in later years, and a requirement that assessors explain residential value increases of 10% or more. Our Iowa homestead exemption guide has the full detail.

How your sale price affects the assessment

Your sale price can become evidence of value for the parcel. When a deed is recorded, the buyer or seller submits a declaration of value to the county recorder, who enters the required data and sends the forms to the assessor. The assessor keeps them three years from December 31 of the transfer year (428A.1).

Because 441.21 tells assessors to consider normal sales and to discount abnormal ones, a sale between relatives or a forced sale is treated differently from an ordinary one. Sellers who think the assessment is too high can use a sale record, the property's condition and nearby sales in an April protest to the board of review. Taxes on an assessment under appeal are still due on schedule, and a reduction is later credited or refunded.

Who owes the tax when an Iowa house is sold?

The tax lien attaches to the parcel, and as against a purchaser it attaches on and after June 30 each year (445.28 and 445.30). Chapter 445 has no proration rule, so the split of the current year's taxes between buyer and seller is a matter for the sale contract and closing statement.

Do these before closing:

  • Ask the county treasurer for the full amount due, any tax sale and any redemption amount. A non-titleholder pays $2 per parcel per year requested (445.23).
  • Keep the statement and the receipt showing full payment, which together are conclusive evidence the parcel was clear on that date, subject to exceptions (445.24).
  • Ask whether a partial payment plan exists. Treasurers may accept partial payments held in the taxpayer's account and applied before each delinquency date (445.36A).

Partial payments cannot replace redemption after a tax sale and do not extend sale deadlines.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Iowa houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

The Iowa tax sale

At the annual sale, each delinquent parcel is offered for the total of tax, interest, fees and costs. The winning bidder is the one who will accept the smallest percentage of the parcel for that amount, with a floor of 1% (446.16).

Mailed notice goes out by regular mail no later than May 1, and failing to receive it is not a defense. If no one bids, the county bids the total due with no cash exchanged (446.19). A parcel tied to a pending municipal infraction citation or certain nuisance petitions cannot be offered (446.7).

The owner keeps the right to redeem. The certificate holder may serve notice of expiration after one year and nine months from the sale, and the right ends 90 days after service is complete (447.9 and 447.12). Redemption interest runs at 2% per month on the sale amount and later taxes (447.1). Notice must reach people with recorded interests, such as mortgagees, contract vendors and the city.

Owner-occupants who cannot pay may petition the board of supervisors, which can order the county to redeem and charge the cost back to the taxing bodies (447.9(3)).

Can a tax bill be reduced after a fire or other casualty?

Sometimes. The board of supervisors may abate or refund taxes on property destroyed by casualty, to the extent insurance does not cover it, if the parcel was not sold for taxes and was not delinquent 30 days before the loss (445.62).

The county may also compromise or abate taxes it holds on tax sale certificates by agreement or resolution (445.16). Owners of damaged houses facing a sale should ask the treasurer whether either rule applies before they set a price.

Selling with taxes owed

Back taxes do not stop a sale. The county treasurer can give you the full amount due, any sale and any redemption figure, and the title company then pays the tax from your proceeds at closing. Start by requesting the statement, because the payoff is easier to plan once you see interest at 1.5% per month on any delinquent installment.

If a tax sale has already happened, check how much of the redemption period is left and what the redemption interest of 2% per month adds. A cash sale that closes before the right to redeem ends lets the payoff come out of your proceeds. Cash Home Buyers purchases houses with delinquent taxes as they stand, with no repairs or cleanup required, and works with the title company on the payoff.

Gather the latest tax statement, any treasurer notices and your parcel number before you ask for an offer.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

When are Iowa property taxes due?

In two installments, with the first half due before September 1 and the second before March 1. They become delinquent on October 1 and April 1.

What is the interest rate on late Iowa property taxes?

Delinquent installments accrue interest at 1.5% per month from the delinquency date, and part of a month counts as a full month.

Does Iowa prorate property tax at closing?

Chapter 445 sets no proration rule. The buyer and seller usually settle it in the purchase contract and closing statement, and the tax lien attaches against purchasers on and after June 30.

How can I find out what is owed on an Iowa parcel?

Ask the county treasurer. The treasurer states the full tax, any tax sales and the redemption amount on request, and mails tax statements to the titleholder.

What is the new Iowa homestead exemption?

It is an exemption equal to 10% of the homestead's taxable value, with a $5,500 minimum and a $20,000 maximum, replacing the old credit starting with assessment year 2026.

title: Iowa Homestead Exemption: Eligibility, Filing and Selling the Home
content:
Iowa Homestead Exemption: Eligibility, Filing and Selling the Home

Cash Home Buyers in Iowa
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Iowa Homestead Exemption: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is
  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Iowa Homestead Exemption sale
  • Turn the Iowa Homestead Exemption offer down and you owe us nothing

Selling a Iowa House? Get a Cash Offer

We buy as-is.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Iowa?
We buy Iowa houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

What changed with the Iowa homestead benefit in 2026

Iowa replaced its homestead tax credit with a homestead exemption equal to 10 percent of the home's taxable value. Senate File 2472, signed May 18, 2026, made the change.

An exemption lowers the value that gets taxed, while a credit comes straight off the bill, and that is the whole difference. Under Iowa Code 425.1, the old credit equaled the levy on the first $4,850 of a home's value, with a floor of $62.50.

The change reaches back to assessment year 2026. You will see it on the bills paid in September 2027 and March 2028.

How much the exemption is worth

The exemption is 10 percent of taxable value, with a minimum of $5,500 and a maximum of $20,000 of taxable value. Starting with assessment years that begin on or after January 1, 2027, the $20,000 maximum is adjusted for inflation.

Exemption featureAmount
Rate10 percent of taxable value
Minimum exemption$5,500 of taxable value
Maximum exemption$20,000 of taxable value in 2026, indexed from 2027
Extra for age 65 and older$6,500 of taxable value
First applies toAssessment year 2026

Owners with a small house get the minimum. The floor lifts the benefit for low-valued houses, and the cap holds it down for expensive ones. What you save in dollars depends on your local levy, because the exemption lowers taxable value rather than the bill itself.

Who qualifies?

You must live in Iowa and occupy the home. The test is living there on July 1 and for at least six months of every year. The extra exemption for older owners requires the owner to be 65 or older on January 1 of the year of the application.

Other points that affect eligibility:

  • Owners already getting the credit before July 1, 2026 are awarded the 10 percent exemption automatically if they still qualify.
  • Owners 65 or older who qualify for the additional exemption do not have to refile each year.
  • The disabled veteran homestead credit remains in place and was not eliminated by the new law.

Iowa also has a military exemption for qualifying service members, including Guard members and reservists, and a family farm credit for tracts of 10 acres or more that are farmed by the owner or immediate family. Each has its own filing rules at the assessor's office.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Iowa house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

How and when to file

The first claim is due on or before July 1 of that year. Use Homestead Tax Exemption form 54-028, available from the Department of Revenue, and submit it to your county assessor.

You file once. The exemption then carries forward until the property is sold or the owner no longer qualifies. The family farm credit runs on a different date, November 1.

A recent buyer should ask the assessor about the July 1 date right away, and a seller can pass that reminder along to the buyer in the final week before closing.

How much land counts toward the homestead?

Homestead covers the house plus up to one-half acre inside a city plat, or up to forty acres outside one.

When a parcel has more land than the limit, the land value is scaled down before the exemption is figured. In the state's example, a two-acre parcel inside a city plat has a $10,000 land value, and that is cut to $2,500 for homestead purposes.

The disabled veteran credit is narrower. For applications submitted on or after July 1, 2026, it covers the dwelling without appurtenances plus one-half acre, whether or not the land is in a plat.

Sellers of rural Iowa houses should look at this closely. A house on an 80-acre parcel is not fully covered, so the tax bill on the whole parcel can look different from a town lot.

Checking your homestead status before you list

Ten minutes with your tax bill can head off a closing-table surprise. Find the homestead line. If it is not there, phone the county assessor and ask what the office wants from you. Nobody who already held the credit should have to reapply, and owners 65 or older never refile, so a missing exemption is worth a call.

Have the parcel number, your target closing date and proof that you live in the home ready when you call. Ask how the exemption will appear on the September 2027 and March 2028 payments, and whether anything on the parcel record needs correcting before a buyer's title company pulls it. A buyer who intends to live in the house files a new application by July 1, so tell them that date early.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Iowa houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What happens to the exemption when you sell

Your exemption stops at closing, and the buyer must apply for theirs.

Expect these at closing:

  • Tax for the year of sale is still billed in two installments, delinquent after September 30 and March 31 (Iowa Code 445.37).
  • Buyer and seller usually split the current installment on the closing statement.
  • Moving out before July 1 can affect whether you meet the occupancy test for that year.

Selling because taxes or repairs have become too much to handle? A cash sale cuts the time you carry the house. Our Iowa property tax guide covers appeals and unpaid taxes.

Other 2026 Iowa property tax changes

The same bill, SF 2472, rewrote other property tax rules, and several reach sellers.

  • Fiscal year 2027 uses a residential rollback of 44.5345 percent.
  • A restored multi-residential class takes in homes with three or more dwelling units on January 1, 2027. Duplexes and single-family homes remain residential.
  • Assessments generally happen every two years.
  • From January 1, 2027, the assessor carries the burden of proof when an assessment rises by more than 10 percent.
  • State funding for the old credit phases out between July 1, 2027 and July 1, 2029.

To protest an assessment, file with the local board of review between April 2 and April 30 (Iowa Code 441.37). A county under a disaster declaration gets a later window, May 1 through June 5.

New Iowa laws that affect a house sale

Two laws effective July 1, 2026 reach ordinary home sales.

  • SF 2448 requires homeowners associations to certify whether dues are current and to disclose approved upcoming assessments and transfer-related fees.
  • When a buyer requests repairs after an inspection, the seller may ask for the matching sections of the report. If the buyer does not supply them, the seller may cancel the contract without penalty.
  • SF 2472 also creates a FirstHome Iowa savings account for first-time buyers to save for down payments and closing costs.

These rules matter most to sellers who list with an agent and haggle over repairs. A direct as-is sale skips the repair-request step entirely.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

How much is the Iowa homestead exemption?

It is 10 percent of your home's taxable value, no less than $5,500 and no more than $20,000 for assessment year 2026. The cap is adjusted for inflation starting with assessment years that begin in 2027.

Do I need to reapply if I already get the Iowa homestead credit?

No. Owners who received the homestead credit or exemption before July 1, 2026 are automatically awarded the 10 percent exemption if they are still eligible.

What is the deadline to claim the Iowa homestead exemption?

July 1 of the year you first claim it. You file Form 54-028 with your county assessor.

Does the homestead exemption transfer to the buyer?

No. It continues only until the property is sold or the owner no longer qualifies, so the new owner must apply on their own.

Is the disabled veteran credit gone?

No. SF 2472 did not eliminate the disabled veteran homestead tax credit. For applications on or after July 1, 2026, it covers the dwelling plus one-half acre.

title: Iowa Estate and Inheritance Tax: What Heirs Owe When Selling
content:
Iowa Estate and Inheritance Tax: What Heirs Owe When Selling

Cash Home Buyers in Iowa
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Iowa Estate and Inheritance Tax: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is
  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Iowa Estate and Inheritance Tax sale
  • Turn the Iowa Estate and Inheritance Tax offer down and you owe us nothing

Selling a Iowa House? Get a Cash Offer

We buy as-is.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Iowa?
We buy Iowa houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

Does Iowa have an estate or inheritance tax?

Neither applies to a person who dies now. The state estate tax ended for deaths on or after January 1, 2005, and the inheritance tax ended for deaths on or after January 1, 2025.

Heirs often mix the two up. An estate tax is charged on the whole estate. Iowa's inheritance tax was based on what each beneficiary had a right to receive, so the rate depended on who the heir was.

Heirs of an Iowa house today face no Iowa death tax return before a sale, and no Iowa tax office needs to sign off first. Other costs remain, and the sections below cover them.

How the inheritance tax was phased out

The Legislature cut the tax in steps over four years and then ended it. Iowa Code 450.10(7) reduced the normal rates by a set percentage depending on the year of death.

Year of deathRate reduction
202120 percent
202240 percent
202360 percent
202480 percent
2025 and laterChapter does not apply

The end point is written into chapter 450, which does not apply to property of estates of decedents dying on or after January 1, 2025. The tax on unknown heirs followed the same schedule and also ended for 2025 deaths.

If the person who owned the house died in 2024 or earlier, the old rules can still matter, so keep reading. Ask the estate attorney or the title company which year applies before you set a closing date.

Who paid inheritance tax before 2025

Close family paid nothing. Property passing to a surviving spouse, parents and grandparents, children, stepchildren, grandchildren and other lineal descendants was exempt under chapter 450.

Everyone else could owe, and the rate climbed with the amount received. These were the brackets before the phase-down reductions:

  • Siblings, sons-in-law and daughters-in-law: 5 percent on the first $12,500, rising by bracket to 10 percent on amounts above $150,000.
  • Other heirs, such as nieces, nephews, cousins and friends: 10 percent up to $50,000, 12 percent to $100,000 and 15 percent above that.
  • Out-of-state charitable bodies: 10 percent on the full amount.
  • For-profit firms and corporations: 15 percent on the full amount.

Some transfers were left out altogether. An estate of $25,000 or less after debts owed no tax, tangible personal property was exempt when the total was $5,000 or less, and gifts to qualifying charitable, educational and religious groups were excluded.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Iowa house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Old inheritance tax deadlines

The tax came due on the last day of the ninth month after the date of death, and the return was due the same day unless none was required. For earlier deaths, the beneficiary was responsible for paying.

The Department of Revenue could extend payment for up to ten years from the end of the month of death to avoid hardship, but interest ran from the original date. Late payment also carried a penalty.

These dates only matter for an older death. A house inherited from someone who died in 2023, for example, can still carry an open file, so check before closing.

Can an old inheritance tax lien affect a sale?

Yes, for deaths before 2025. Iowa Code 450.7 made the tax a lien on the taxable estate and the decedent's property from the date of death until paid, and a sale did not wipe it out.

The lien generally ends ten years after death. It ranks ahead of later mortgages, buyers and judgment creditors without any recorded notice. Property passing to a spouse, parents, children and other lineal descendants was never subject to it.

Clearing the lien took one of these filings:

  • Filing a receipt showing the tax was paid with the clerk of court.
  • Filing a certificate that no tax was owed.
  • Filing a release or waiver.
  • Where no return was required, filing an affidavit describing the real estate in the county where it sits (section 450.22).

A title company or estate attorney usually handles the paperwork. Heirs selling after a pre-2025 death should ask whether anything is still open of record.

The federal estate tax

The federal tax touches only very large estates. Its filing threshold is $15,000,000 for 2026 deaths, compared with $13,990,000 for 2025.

Gross estate plus adjusted taxable gifts plus the specific gift tax exemption above the threshold means a federal return is due. A surviving spouse can also elect to carry over the unused exemption of the person who died, by filing a timely estate tax return.

Nearly every Iowa family inheriting a house sits far under that line, and the house is only one asset in the total.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Iowa houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Property taxes that follow an inherited home

A death tax or not, the county still bills property tax. Installments are delinquent on October 1 and April 1 (Iowa Code 445.37). If the last day of September or March lands on a weekend, delinquency starts on the second business day of the following month.

The homestead benefit does not ride along with the house. It ends when the property is sold or the owner stops qualifying, so an heir who will not move in may be taxed without it. Our Iowa homestead exemption guide covers the 2026 change.

Mind the calendar. A cash buyer can often close before a due date, and the settlement statement shows what is paid from proceeds.

Selling an inherited house in Iowa

How you sell turns on who holds title and whether the court has an open estate. Will or no will, the person with authority over the estate signs the deed, and the title company asks to see that authority in writing.

Iowa transfer tax comes due when the deed is recorded: eighty cents for every $500 of value past the first $500 (Iowa Code 428A.1). You pay it to the county recorder and file a declaration of value with the deed. A transfer for no consideration owes nothing.

  • Get the death certificate and any will together.
  • Decide who can sign: an executor, or heirs who hold title.
  • Order a lien search from the title company, including any inheritance tax lien from before 2025.
  • Look up the next property tax installment.

Cash Home Buyers buys inherited Iowa houses in their current condition, which suits heirs who do not want to pay for repairs. A cash sale means no showings and no wait on a buyer's loan approval, so the heirs can pick a closing date. For deaths in 2025 or later no Iowa inheritance tax return comes first. The paperwork is mostly the deed, the proof of authority and the title search.

Frequently asked questions

Is there an inheritance tax in Iowa in 2026?

No. The inheritance tax does not apply to deaths on or after January 1, 2025, so a 2026 death creates no Iowa inheritance tax return.

Does Iowa have a state estate tax?

No. The Iowa estate tax does not apply to deaths on or after January 1, 2005. The federal estate tax is separate and has a 2026 filing threshold of $15,000,000.

Do I owe Iowa inheritance tax if my parent died in 2024?

A child inheriting from a parent owed nothing, because property passing to children and other lineal descendants was exempt under chapter 450. Siblings and other heirs could owe a tax at rates reduced by 80 percent for 2024 deaths.

Can an inheritance tax lien block a sale of the house?

It can for older deaths. The lien under section 450.7 generally ends ten years after death, but it can be released earlier by a receipt, certificate or waiver, and a title company can tell you whether one is on record.

Do heirs keep the homestead exemption on an inherited Iowa house?

Not automatically. The exemption continues only while the owner still qualifies, and it ends when the property is sold.

title: Iowa Sheriff Sales: Foreclosure Sale Steps and Redemption
content:
Iowa Sheriff Sales: Foreclosure Sale Steps and Redemption

  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Iowa Sheriff Sales sale
  • Turn the Iowa Sheriff Sales offer down and you owe us nothing

Selling a Iowa House? Get a Cash Offer

We buy as-is.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Iowa?
We buy Iowa houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.

How an Iowa sheriff sale works

A sheriff sale is a public auction of property after a court has ordered it sold to pay a debt. The county sheriff runs it. For a home loan, the road to the auction goes through district court, because Iowa mortgages are foreclosed by a court action in equity, with one narrow exception for a voluntary agreement (Iowa Code chapter 654).

The court enters judgment for the full amount due and orders the property sold as needed to satisfy it. The sale then happens under a special execution. Whether the former owner gets a redemption period afterward depends on which kind of foreclosure the lender chose.

Other creditors can end up at a sheriff sale too, since Iowa enforces money judgments by execution against real estate. Chapter 626 sets the notice and auction rules for both situations.

Notices required before a lender can sell

Before a lender files, Iowa requires specific notices, and they differ by property type. A skipped notice is often the first thing an owner's attorney checks.

  • One- and two-family residences: a written notice of the right to cure, giving thirty days from the notice to bring the loan current, with no acceleration until that time runs out (section 654.2D). There is no cure right if a proper notice went out for a default within the previous 365 days.
  • Farmland: a notice of right to cure and a 45-day wait before enforcement (section 654.2A). For farm debt of $20,000 or more, a mediation release is generally needed first (sections 654.2C and 654A.11).
  • Owner-occupied homes: the lender must tell the owner about counseling and mediation on a form the attorney general prescribes. To qualify for attorney fees, the lender must also give a fourteen-day demand for payment of the accelerated balance (section 654.4B).

If the court finds the counseling notice was never served and the owner asks for counseling or mediation, the sale can be delayed, though never beyond sixty days (section 654.4B).

Notice of the sale itself

Real estate sold by a sheriff needs four weeks of notice, posted and published. The main timing rules:

  • Notice period: four weeks before the sale (626.74).
  • Posting: at least three public places in the county, one of them the courthouse (626.75).
  • Newspaper: first publication at least four weeks before the sale (626.75).
  • Occupying debtor: written notice served at least twenty days before the sale (626.78).
  • Auction hours: between 9:00 a.m. and 4:00 p.m. (626.80).
  • Junior creditor request: proof of service filed at least ten days before the sale (654.15A).

A sheriff who sells without the required notice forfeits $100 to the defendant plus actual damages, but the sale itself stands (section 626.77). A sale made without the twenty-day notice to an occupying debtor can be set aside on motion within ninety days (section 626.79). The statutes are on the Iowa Legislature site.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Iowa house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

How does the auction itself work?

The sheriff sells at public auction between 9:00 a.m. and 4:00 p.m., and the notice must carry the start time and place. The statute names no single location, so the notice is where to look.

Sealed written bids are allowed. The sheriff receipts them, keeps them sealed until the auction begins, then opens and announces them. If a winning written bidder does not pay in certified funds as the notice directs, the bid is canceled and the sheriff certifies the next highest bidder, within 24 hours for an electronic transfer or 48 hours otherwise (section 626.80).

The sale can be postponed when there are no bidders, when the offer is grossly inadequate, when the judgment creditor asks, or when the parties agree. Without a written agreement, no more than two adjournments of up to sixty days each are allowed (section 626.81).

Two more details help owners. A debtor can deliver a signed plan of division before 9:00 a.m. on the sale day so that only the land needed to cover the debt is sold (section 626.84). And money left after the debt and costs goes to the debtor, unless another execution or valid lien claims it (section 626.82).

Redemption after the sale

The default is one year from the day of sale, and the owner keeps possession in the meantime. The first six months belong to the debtor alone (section 628.3). If the debtor does not redeem, a mortgagee or qualifying creditor may redeem within nine months of the sale (section 628.5).

Shorter periods apply in several situations. Compare the table with your court papers.

SituationRedemption periodSection
Standard saleOne year; debtor alone for six months628.3
Mortgage under 10 acres, if the mortgage provides and the lender waives a deficiencySix months, or three months if not agricultural628.26
Under 10 acres, abandoned, mortgage provides, deficiency waivedSixty days628.27
Non-agricultural, non-residential property180 days; 90 days with a deficiency waiver628.28
Former one- or two-family residence the debtor no longer occupies30 days, or 60 with junior creditors628.28
Foreclosure without redemption elected by the plaintiffNone after the sale654.23

Redeeming a sold home frees it from liability for any unpaid judgment balance (section 628.3). The periods differ a lot, so the dates in the decree and the sheriff's certificate control.

Foreclosure without redemption

On property not used for agriculture, the plaintiff can elect to skip the post-sale redemption period (sections 654.20 through 654.23). The petition must carry a required notice on its first page.

The owner can respond by filing a demand to delay the sale before judgment. The sale then comes two months after judgment, six months for a one- or two-family residence, or three months if the petition waives a deficiency judgment (section 654.21). With no demand, the sale is held promptly after judgment.

Once the sale happens, the mortgagor has no right to redeem, and junior lienholders lose theirs as well. When someone other than the mortgagee buys, junior liens are extinguished (section 654.23). For a one- or two-family residence with no deficiency waiver and no demand for delay, the plaintiff cannot seek a deficiency judgment (section 654.26).

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Iowa houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What happens to the people living in the house?

The owner stays through the redemption period. Once it ends and a deed issues, a court order can remove the former owner. A defendant who stays after a foreclosure or execution sale faces forcible entry and detainer, unless that person claims paramount title (section 648.1).

  • Written notice to quit: three days before suing (section 648.3).
  • Hearing: set no later than 8 days from filing, or 15 if the plaintiff asks or agrees to a later date (section 648.5).
  • Removal: the execution issues within 3 days of judgment and can be carried out only in the daytime (sections 648.20 and 648.22).

Those steps run on short clocks, so an owner who wants to choose how the house changes hands has the most room before the sale date.

Selling before the sheriff sale

An owner can generally sell to a buyer at any point before the auction, as long as the sale pays what the judgment and liens require. A closing before the auction can end the case without a sheriff's deed.

Iowa law offers a few related paths. During a pending foreclosure, the plaintiff may ask the court to approve a commercially reasonable sale free of liens, with net proceeds held in escrow (section 654.17A). Before a sheriff's deed is recorded, the judgment creditor may rescind the foreclosure by filing a notice and a $50 fee (section 654.17). A voluntary nonjudicial foreclosure under section 654.18 takes a written agreement from both sides, and the mortgagor gets a five-business-day right to cancel.

The seller of an Iowa house owes the state transfer tax, 80 cents for each $500 of value above the first $500 (sections 428A.1 and 428A.3).

If you want to sell, gather the judgment or decree, the sheriff's notice, your loan payoff figure and a list of every lien. Cash Home Buyers can look at an Iowa house as-is while a foreclosure is pending, and you decide whether the numbers work. Talk with an Iowa attorney about your own case first, since the dates in your decree are what count.

Frequently asked questions

Who runs an Iowa sheriff sale?

The sheriff of the county where the property sits. The sale follows a court judgment, and the notice sets the date, start time and place.

How many weeks of notice does Iowa require for a sheriff sale?

Four weeks. The notice goes up in at least three public places in the county, including the courthouse, and is published in a newspaper with the first run at least four weeks before the sale.

Can the owner stay in the house after the sheriff sale?

Usually yes, during the redemption period. The period can be as short as 30 days in some cases, and there is none when the plaintiff elected foreclosure without redemption.

Is there a deficiency judgment after an Iowa foreclosure?

Sometimes. If the sale falls short, a general execution may issue against the mortgagor unless the parties agreed otherwise. A one- or two-family residence with no deficiency waiver and no demand for delay is protected (sections 654.6 and 654.26).

Can a sheriff sale be postponed?

Yes. The sheriff can postpone for no bidders, a grossly inadequate offer, or a request from the judgment creditor. Without written agreement, the limit is two adjournments of up to sixty days each.

title: Iowa Quitclaim Deed: Recording, Fees and When It Works
content:
Iowa Quitclaim Deed: Recording, Fees and When It Works

Cash Home Buyers in Iowa
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Iowa Quitclaim Deed: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is
  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Iowa Quitclaim Deed sale
  • Turn the Iowa Quitclaim Deed offer down and you owe us nothing

Selling a Iowa House? Get a Cash Offer

We buy as-is.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Iowa?
We buy Iowa houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

What an Iowa quitclaim deed transfers

A quitclaim deed hands over whatever interest the signer holds, and promises nothing beyond that. Iowa Code 558.19 gives a sample quitclaim form: it names a consideration in dollars and says the grantor quitclaims to the grantee all interest in a described tract.

The same statute has sample forms for a fee simple deed without warranty, which uses the words "hereby convey," and for a warranty deed, which adds a warranty of title against all persons. Each form is sufficient if varied to suit the circumstances, so the quitclaim is a valid way to move title. What changes is the promise the grantor makes.

For that reason a quitclaim suits transfers between people who already know the property's history, such as adding a spouse or placing a house into a family arrangement. It is a poor fit when a stranger is paying money and wants a promise about title.

Recording costs at the county recorder

Recording usually runs $5 per page plus two $1 charges, and transfer tax can be added if money changed hands. The recorder's schedule comes from Iowa Code 331.604.

ChargeAmount
Recording a real estate instrument$5 per page or fraction, per transaction
Records management fund$1 per recorded transaction
Electronic transaction fund$1 per recorded transaction
Transfer tax80 cents per $500 or fraction over the first $500 of consideration
Groundwater hazard statementNo recorder fee

Some counties add services or rules of their own, so phone the recorder before you mail a deed.

How should the deed be formatted for the recorder?

Each recorder sets its own format rules. The Story County Recorder publishes a clear list, which makes a handy model. Its deeds need:

  • At least three inches of blank space at the top of the first page.
  • The preparer's name, address and phone number typed directly below that space.
  • The line "Address Tax Statement To" with the taxpayer's name and address, right under the preparer information.
  • A full legal description, never the shortened one printed on a tax statement.
  • Printed names beneath every signature, including the acknowledging officer.
  • A signed, dated and notarized document that is legible and reproducible.

Other counties vary in small ways. The Story County recording requirements page has the full list.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Iowa house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Notarizing the deed, including remote notarization

A deed has to be acknowledged before a notarial officer to be lawfully recorded (558.42), and the acknowledgment follows Chapter 9B (558.20). The signer declares that the signature is theirs and was given for the stated purpose. An entity signer must have authority.

The officer confirms identity through personal knowledge or satisfactory evidence. Good evidence includes a passport, driver's license or government nondriver ID that is current or expired no more than three years, or a credible witness. The officer can refuse to proceed if unsure that the signer has capacity or is signing knowingly and voluntarily.

Remote notarization is allowed under 9B.14A. Notary and signer must communicate by sight and sound. Identity needs personal knowledge, a credible witness or two types of identity proofing. The notary makes an audio-visual recording and keeps it for at least ten years, and the certificate must say technology was used. Ask the recorder whether the county will accept the resulting document.

When a quitclaim deed owes Iowa transfer tax

Transfer tax applies only when consideration is above $500. The rate is 80 cents for each $500 or fraction over $500, and the person conveying the property owes it (428A.1 and 428A.3).

Many family and court-driven transfers are exempt under 428A.2. The exemptions most likely to touch a quitclaim are:

  • Deeds between spouses, or between parent and child, without actual consideration. Cancelling debt secured by the property is not actual consideration if it stays within the property's fair market value.
  • Deeds between former spouses under a dissolution decree.
  • Deeds that correct, confirm or supplement a recorded deed with no added consideration.
  • Deeds returning property to lienholders in lieu of foreclosure.
  • Deeds distributing trust assets to beneficiaries without consideration.

A recorder will not accept an exempt deed without a signed statement claiming the exemption, filed with the deed or endorsed on it (428A.4). Knowingly skipping tax that is due, or willfully entering false information on a declaration of value, is a simple misdemeanor (428A.10 and 428A.15).

Declaration of value and groundwater hazard statement

Both forms travel with the deed. The declaration of value reports the full consideration. At least one seller or buyer, or an agent, must sign it, and it is required unless the deed falls in an exempt category. The recorder does not record it; the data goes to the assessor (428A.1).

The groundwater hazard statement under 558.69 covers known burial sites, wells, solid waste disposal sites, underground storage tanks, hazardous waste and private sewage systems. The owner is responsible for getting it right. If none of those conditions exist, the first page of the deed carries the exemption statement. A recorder must refuse a deed missing the required statement, though a deed recorded without it is not void.

The groundwater process has worked differently since July 1, 2022 (House File 2343), so use the current form from the recorder.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Iowa houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Does a spouse have to sign?

Often yes. When the owner is married, conveying the homestead is not valid unless the other spouse signs the same or a like instrument, or a power of attorney for it (561.13).

A spouse who holds only homestead rights and a statutory share can relinquish those rights specifically under 597.5 without joining the granting clause. The signature requirement does not apply if a dissolution decree ended the interest, if the right of recovery is barred under 614.15, for a purchase-money mortgage, or where a court of equity finds that undoing the transaction would unjustly enrich the other spouse.

The homestead is the owner's home plus the contiguous land used with it. Inside a city plat it is capped at one half acre, and outside a plat at forty acres (561.1 and 561.2).

When a quitclaim is the wrong tool for selling

An unrecorded instrument is invalid against later good-faith purchasers for value without notice, so recording promptly protects the new owner (558.41). Quitclaim transfers are also excluded from the seller disclosure requirement, one reason families use them between relatives.

Other recording rules depend on the property. Entity transfers carry implied warranties unless the deed says otherwise, including that the entity exists and the signer is authorized (558.72). A grantee of agricultural land must record within 180 days (558.44).

If you plan to sell, ask the buyer or title company which form they want before you sign anything. A buyer paying cash will usually expect a warranty or a title policy behind the deed. Owners with liens, back taxes or unclear co-owners should get advice first, since a quitclaim does not clear any of those problems; it only passes along what the signer owns.

A practical order of steps: pull the current deed, confirm every owner on it, get payoff figures for any loans, then decide on the form. Bring the deed, photo ID for each signer and the legal description to the notary appointment, and have the declaration of value filled out before the recorder sees the packet.

Frequently asked questions

Is a quitclaim deed legal in Iowa?

Yes. Iowa Code 558.19 lists the quitclaim form beside fee simple deeds without warranty and with warranty as sufficient ways to convey.

What does it cost to record an Iowa quitclaim deed?

Recording is $5 per page or fraction, plus $1 for the records management fund and $1 for the electronic transaction fund per recorded transaction. Transfer tax applies only if consideration exceeds $500.

Does a quitclaim deed need to be notarized in Iowa?

Yes. A deed must be acknowledged under Chapter 9B before it can be lawfully recorded. Remote notarization is allowed when the statutory conditions are met.

Does a quitclaim deed remove my spouse's homestead rights?

Not by itself. A married owner's homestead conveyance is invalid without the spouse's signature on the same or a like instrument, with limited exceptions.

Can I quitclaim my house to my child without paying transfer tax in Iowa?

A deed between parent and child without actual consideration is exempt under 428A.2. You must claim the exemption in a signed statement, and recording fees still apply.

title: Iowa Capital Gains Tax When You Sell a House
content:
Iowa Capital Gains Tax When You Sell a House

Cash Home Buyers in Iowa
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Iowa Capital Gains Tax When You Sell a House: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is
  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Iowa Capital Gains Tax When You Sell a House sale
  • Turn the Iowa Capital Gains Tax When You Sell a House offer down and you owe us nothing

Selling a Iowa House? Get a Cash Offer

We buy as-is.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Iowa?
We buy Iowa houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

Does Iowa tax capital gains on a house sale?

Not with a separate tax. Profit from selling a house is reported on your Iowa individual income tax return, and for tax year 2026 one flat rate of 3.8 percent applies to every level of taxable income.

On the Iowa return, the capital gain or loss line starts from 100 percent of the amount on your federal Form 1040. The capital gain deduction is not taken on that line, because a qualifying deduction goes on its own line. If your federal return needs Schedule D and Form 8949, a copy goes with the Iowa return.

Do not confuse two 3.8 percent figures. The Iowa rate and the federal net investment income tax share a number and nothing else. They are separate taxes with separate rules, and both can matter on a large gain.

The home sale exclusion

A house that was your main home qualifies for an exclusion of up to $250,000 in gain, or up to $500,000 when you file jointly. Iowa generally follows the federal rules on excluding gain from a principal residence, so the federal exclusion also keeps that gain off your Iowa taxable income.

You have to pass two tests:

  • Ownership: you or your spouse held title for at least 24 months within the five years ending at the sale.
  • Use: you, and your spouse on a joint return, each used it as a main home for 24 months or more inside that same window.

The two stretches can fall in different months. Taking the exclusion on another home sale during the prior two years usually rules it out. IRS Publication 523 covers exceptions and partial exclusions.

A Form 1099-S in your mailbox means the sale gets reported, even if all of the gain is excludable. The same goes when only part of the gain can be excluded; use Form 8949 with Schedule D.

When the gain is bigger than the exclusion

Gain above the exclusion is taxed federally as a capital gain and in Iowa at the flat state rate. The federal rate depends on how long you held the property.

SituationTax treatment
Held one year or lessShort-term, taxed as ordinary income
Held more than one yearLong-term, federal rates of 0, 15 or 20 percent by taxable income
Unrecaptured section 1250 gain (depreciation on real property)Maximum federal rate of 25 percent
Iowa individual income tax, 20263.8 percent flat
Iowa interest on overdue tax, from January 1, 202610 percent a year, 0.8 percent a month

The federal net investment income tax is 3.8 percent for single filers above $200,000, joint filers above $250,000 and separate filers above $125,000 of modified adjusted gross income. It does not apply to the part of a home sale gain that is excluded as a principal residence, but gain above the exclusion can be hit.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Iowa house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Repealed Iowa capital gain deductions

Most Iowa capital gain deductions ended with tax year 2023. Repealed categories include gains from selling real estate used in a non-farm business, an entire business, timber, cattle, horses or breeding livestock (with an exception for retired farmers), and employer securities sold to a qualified Iowa employee stock ownership plan.

The change took effect January 1, 2023. Installment sales that began before that date still qualify for the deduction. Some older reference material for non-farm real property is still around, and the 2023 changes control.

If you read older guidance that gave a ten-year holding rule for business real estate, ignore it. A rental or commercial property sold after 2022 does not get that deduction.

  • Retired farmers aged 55 or older may still deduct gain from farm real estate if they materially participated in farming for ten years in total.
  • A retired farmer has a single lifetime election.
  • Electing the deduction blocks the beginning farmer tax credit and the farm lease income exclusion.
  • Gain from an employee-owned corporation's stock has its own phase-in: 33 percent excluded for 2023, 66 percent for 2024 and 100 percent from 2025.

A house in town or a rental house falls outside those farm rules. A principal residence relies on the federal exclusion.

Selling an inherited house

An heir's tax basis usually resets to the home's fair market value at the date of death, instead of what the deceased paid. For that reason a sale soon after inheriting often leaves little or no taxable gain.

The personal representative may choose an alternate valuation date and use the value then. Without a Schedule A (Form 8971), you can fall back on the appraised value at death for state inheritance or transmission tax purposes. A home given to the decedent within one year before death can keep the decedent's adjusted basis rather than the death-date value.

Hold on to an appraisal from the date of death. It is the first paper a preparer asks for, and it is hard to recreate later.

Do nonresidents owe Iowa tax on a house they sell in Iowa?

Yes, once the Iowa-source income reaches the filing trigger. Capital gain on the sale of Iowa property counts as income from Iowa property, along with rental income. A nonresident or part-year resident must file when Iowa-source net income is $1,000 or more, unless income falls under the standard thresholds.

For the 2025 return year those thresholds were more than $9,000 for single or married filing separately filers, and more than $13,500 for joint filers, head of household and qualifying surviving spouse. Higher amounts apply to people 65 and older.

Owners who sell an Iowa house after moving away, and heirs living out of state, often miss this step. Look into it before the sale money is spent.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Iowa houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Other costs when you sell an Iowa house

Iowa property tax and state transfer tax are separate from any income tax on the gain. Real estate transfer tax applies to a deed that conveys Iowa real estate when the consideration exceeds $500, at 80 cents for each $500 or fractional part above $500 (Iowa Code 428A.1). The full price counts as consideration, including any lien the buyer assumes.

  • A declaration of value, signed by at least one buyer or seller, goes to the county recorder with the deed.
  • Personal property is presumed part of the price unless its value is stated on the instrument.
  • Property tax on Iowa homes runs a year behind and is billed in September and March.
  • A seller closing from July 1 to December 31 owes the September installment, and one closing from January 1 to June 30 owes the March one.

An as-is cash sale leaves these rules unchanged. What changes is who pays for repairs and how fast the deal closes. Before you sign, ask the title company to list each tax and fee that will come out of your proceeds, and talk with a tax preparer about the gain itself.

Frequently asked questions

Is there a capital gains tax in Iowa?

Iowa has no separate capital gains tax. Gains are part of Iowa taxable income, which is taxed at a flat 3.8 percent for tax year 2026.

Do I pay Iowa tax on the sale of my primary residence?

Only on gain above the exclusion. Iowa generally follows the federal rule that lets you exclude up to $250,000, or $500,000 on a joint return, if you meet the ownership and use tests.

Can I deduct capital gains on a rental house sold in Iowa?

Not under the old non-farm real property deduction. It was repealed for tax years starting January 1, 2023, apart from installment sales begun before then.

Does Iowa tax gain when I inherit and sell a house?

Gain is measured from the stepped-up basis, usually the fair market value at the date of death. If you sell at about that value, little gain results.

Do I owe Iowa tax if I sold an Iowa house after moving out of state?

Possibly. Gain on Iowa property is Iowa-source income, and a nonresident must file when Iowa-source net income is $1,000 or more.

content:
Iowa Probate Process and Selling Inherited Property

Cash Home Buyers in Iowa
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Iowa Probate Process and Selling Inherited Property: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is
  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Iowa Probate Process and Selling Inherited Property sale
  • Turn the Iowa Probate Process and Selling Inherited Property offer down and you owe us nothing

Selling a Iowa House? Get a Cash Offer

We buy as-is.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Iowa?
We buy Iowa houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

Does every Iowa house go through probate?

No. An estate does not have to be opened for every person who dies. One may be needed to transfer property, pay debts or obtain tax clearances, and a house titled only in the decedent's name usually needs some court step before it can be sold or retitled.

Probate in Iowa runs through the district court in the county, and the clerk of court is the first office to call. A valid will must be in writing, signed by the maker and witnessed by two people. If you cannot find a will, ask the clerk in the county where it may be stored, any attorney who drafted it, and the named executor, and check safe deposit boxes.

Who can open an Iowa estate, and how soon?

A surviving spouse, an heir, a creditor or another person with good grounds may petition for appointment. Iowa Code 633.227 and 633.228 give priority by class: the surviving spouse has 20 days from the death to file, and each other class has 10 days, with a class's window moving up if nobody exists in the class before it.

Whoever serves must be a natural person of full age, not incompetent and not found unsuitable by the court (633.63). "Full age" means 18, or having married (633.3). A court can remove a fiduciary on a verified petition under 633.65.

With several heirs, agree early on who will be the personal representative. That person signs the sale papers and answers to the court.

Estate deadlines and costs

The statute sets several clocks that matter to a family planning to sell a house.

Estate stepDeadline or cost
Hearing noticeAt least 20 days after service, unless good cause shortens it
Inventory and report90 days after the personal representative qualifies, unless extended
Creditor claimsLater of four months after the second published notice or one month after mailed notice
Spouse's electionFour months after service of notice
Court cost0.2% of probate assets listed in the inventory
Outside limit for openingClaims are barred if administration has not started within five years of death
Delinquent filingsClerk notices go out June 1 and December 1; 60 days to file

The 0.2% court cost leaves out joint tenancy property, lifetime transfers, life insurance payable to a beneficiary and real estate outside Iowa. The sections are 633.40, 633.361, 633.410, 633.237, 633.31, 633.413 and 633.32, in table order.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Iowa house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Who inherits an Iowa house with no will?

Iowa intestacy law sends the house first to a surviving spouse, then down a list of relatives. The split depends on whether the children are also the spouse's children.

  • No children, or all children shared with the spouse: the spouse takes the real property the decedent held during the marriage, subject to exceptions such as judicial sales (633.211).
  • Some children are not the spouse's: the spouse takes one half of the real property, and the estate tops up the spouse's total to $50,000 if the share falls short (633.212).
  • No spouse: the order runs to children, then parents, then siblings' descendants, then grandparents, then great-grandparents, and finally escheat to the state (633.219).

In an intestate estate the spouse may elect a life estate in the homestead instead (633.240). A homestead inside a city plat is limited to one half acre, and outside a plat to forty acres (561.2).

When the personal representative can sell the house

The personal representative can sell estate real estate to pay debts, distribute the estate or serve the estate's best interests. Exempt personal property and the homestead are carved out and follow their own rules (633.386). If the homestead is not set off to the spouse and the spouse has not chosen to occupy it, it can be sold under the court-directed provisions.

Know these features of a sale before you speak with a buyer:

  • Notice of a sale petition goes to interested persons unless they waive it in writing or all of them are personal representatives who signed the petition (633.389).
  • A sale on credit for more than twelve months needs a hearing on notice (633.392).
  • A public auction is advertised once a week for two consecutive weeks in a county newspaper, with the last notice one to seven days before the sale (633.397).
  • Sale proceeds are held by the personal representative, subject to any rights of the spouse or children, unless those rights are waived (633.386).

A title company or buyer may ask the representative to prove authority. Under 633.78, a third party has 10 business days to verify a fiduciary's authority, and an unjustified refusal can lead to penalties from $500 to $10,000 plus damages.

The small estate affidavit and a house

Iowa's affidavit procedure for very small estates applies only if the decedent's personal property totals $50,000 or less and there is no real property. A house is real property, so this shortcut rarely works for a family that wants to sell one.

The procedure also requires that at least forty days have gone by since the death, a sworn affidavit and a certified death certificate, and it cannot be used while an administration is pending (633.356). For deaths before January 1, 2025, real property passing to people exempt from inheritance tax as joint tenants with survivorship rights also qualified.

If the house was held in joint tenancy with a surviving owner, no probate may be needed to move title. Ask the county recorder or an attorney what filing proves the survivor's ownership.

Creditor claims and a house sale

Creditors have a limited window to file, and that window shapes when an estate can safely close. Notice is published once a week for two weeks in a local newspaper, and known claimants whose claims may not be paid in administration receive mailed notice (633.230).

Claims not filed by the later of four months after the second publication or one month after mailing are barred, with statutory exceptions (633.410). The representative may still pay valid debts that were never filed, at the representative's own risk (633.435). Property other than the homestead and exempt property is chargeable with the debts and costs of the estate (633.350).

Heirs who want a fast sale should talk to the estate's attorney before distributing money. A house sold early can pay the debts, and the remainder can be shared.

Does Iowa still have an inheritance tax?

No tax applies to estates of people who died on or after January 1, 2025. Section 450.98 says the chapter does not apply to the property of those decedents.

The old rules still matter for deaths before 2025. Spouses, lineal ascendants and descendants and stepchildren were exempt. Brothers, sisters and in-laws paid graduated rates from 5% to 10%, and other individuals paid 10% to 15%. The tax was due nine months after death and was a lien on the estate for up to ten years. A sale by a personal representative under a will's power or a court order removed the lien from the property and moved it to the proceeds (450.6, 450.7, 450.10).

For an older death, ask whether a receipt or certificate of nonliability was filed with the clerk of court.

Options for selling an inherited Iowa house

An heir with legal authority can list the house on the open market, sell it at auction under court rules, or accept an as-is cash offer. Each route requires the same proof of who may sign.

A cash buyer can often close quickly, which suits families who live out of state or share a house among siblings. Whichever buyer you choose, confirm the following in writing:

  • Letters of appointment, or proof that survivorship title passed.
  • Whether the will gives a power of sale, which changes the court steps.
  • Property tax status and any special assessments.
  • Who will receive proceeds, and in what order creditors are paid.

Cash Home Buyers buys inherited houses as they are, so heirs do not have to clean out, repair or stage the home before closing. Gather the letters of appointment, the death certificate and the latest tax statement first, and the title company can tell you what else it needs.

Frequently asked questions

How long does probate take in Iowa?

Length varies. Main checkpoints include the 90-day inventory deadline after the personal representative qualifies and a creditor claim window of at least four months. Most estates with a house last longer than those checkpoints, depending on sales and disputes.

Can an Iowa heir sell a house before probate ends?

Yes, if the personal representative has authority to sell and follows the court or will provisions. A will that gives a power of sale changes the procedure, and a buyer will want letters of appointment.

Is there a small estate shortcut for a house in Iowa?

Usually no. The affidavit for very small estates requires $50,000 or less in personal property and no real property. A house is real property, so formal administration is likely.

Does Iowa charge inheritance tax now?

Not for deaths on or after January 1, 2025. Estates of people who died earlier may still involve the old tax and lien rules.

What does an Iowa probate cost in court fees?

The court cost under Iowa Code 633.31 is 0.2% of the probate assets listed in the inventory for most estate services. It leaves out joint tenancy property, lifetime transfers and life insurance payable to a named beneficiary. Attorney and fiduciary fees are separate costs of administration.
